data.title: Message Consumer
data.tagline: A message consumer is an application or instance that receives messages from a queue, handles them according to its rules, and acknowledges their processing status
data.learningOutcome: You can locate the consumer in the send, receive, process, and acknowledge path, and use buildup and redelivery to judge it.
data.description: An upload API can publish a transcoding task while a consumer takes it from the queue and runs the work. An order system can use a consumer to receive an order-created message and create a shipping record. Without a consumer, messages build up; if processing fails, a message may be delivered again, so successful publishing is not business completion.

learning.assumes: You know an application can hand work to a message queue first.
learning.outcome: You can locate the consumer in the send, receive, process, and acknowledge path, and use buildup and redelivery to judge it.

distinctions.label: Enqueue
distinctions.explanation: Enqueue is the producer operation placing tasks into a queue; a Message Consumer is the background worker picking up and processing queued tasks.

explanation.title: Locate the source of buildup
explanation.text: The producer only sends a message to the queue. If no consumer is running, or consumers are slower than publishing, messages keep accumulating.

explanation.title: Acknowledge after processing
explanation.text: The consumer runs the handler and acknowledges success. On failure, the system can redeliver or record the failure under its rules instead of pretending the work finished.

explanation.title: Judge improvement by evidence
explanation.text: A simulated message should show publish, delivery, processing, and result feedback in logs or status, while buildup falls. A consumer is not the queue; one application can also publish.

data.boundary: Successful publishing is not completed consumption, and an acknowledgement does not by itself make business side effects impossible to repeat. Check consumer health, processing failures, and redelivery rules.

lessonPractice.title: The producer reports success, but the queue keeps growing. What should you inspect first?

options.label: Check whether consumers are online, receiving messages, failing, and reporting results
options.feedback: Correct. Producer success only means the message entered the queue; buildup can come from no consumer or slow processing.

options.label: Have the producer resend the same messages until the queue shrinks
options.feedback: Resending increases buildup and does not show that a consumer received or processed the messages.

options.label: Clear the queue so the monitoring number looks normal again
options.feedback: Clearing can discard unprocessed work and avoids checking the consumer or the failure cause.

data.agentPrompt: Inspect the consumer for this message queue: confirm it starts and keeps receiving messages, reports successful processing, and requeues or records failures instead of silently losing them. Simulate one message and verify the full path from publish to delivery, processing, and result feedback.
